study_type.nlm: Other (quantitative Bayesian causal modelling on synthetic simulation data)
study_type.value: Other (simulation; Bayesian structural causal model on synthetic data)

research_method.claude: Simulation: Bayesian structural causal model (DAG + Bayesian network) estimated on synthetic data (Bayesian and frequentist learning, MCMC, EM), do-operator intervention analysis, scenario modelling, comparison with linear regression and random forest
research_method.nlm: Quantitative Bayesian structural causal modelling on a synthetic dataset; DAG, Bayesian network, do-calculus interventions; fit metrics (log-likelihood, AIC, BIC, CV-10, MAE, RMSE); comparison with linear regression and random forest baselines
research_method.value: Simulation: Bayesian structural causal model (DAG/Bayesian network) linking five DX variables and two controls to release cycle duration, estimated on a synthetic dataset; do-operator intervention scenarios on P(RCD > 14 days); fit via log-likelihood, AIC/BIC, 10-fold CV, MAE/RMSE; comparison with linear regression and random forest baselines
research_method.note: Synthetic dataset size not reported by either.

context.claude: simulated; prototypical cloud CI/CD infrastructure (microservices or serverless); no real organization, team or project
context.nlm: simulated; cloud / full-stack web development environment with CI/CD microservices and serverless architectures
context.value: not reported (simulated; prototypical cloud CI/CD environment with microservices or serverless architecture; synthetic data, no real teams)

dora_applied.note: DORA cited as industry benchmark and criticized as correlational.

ai_discussed.note: Borderline: both extractors list 'uses AI/ML: Yes' only for the Bayesian network / causal-ML libraries used as the statistical analysis method; ChatGPT used only for language editing; MLOps only as future work. AI is not a topic of the study.

cat_productivity.note: No output/throughput metric; target is release cycle duration (delivery).

cat_quality.note: Borderline: both tag Documentation Quality (K) partly as Quality (NLM also code-review feedback), but these are DX input ratings, not defect/stability/maintainability metrics.

cat_collaboration.note: Communication Quality (C) and Feedback from Code Review (F) modelled as variables (synthetic values).

cat_satisfaction.note: Developer Tooling Satisfaction (B); Claude also reports a Developer Satisfaction Index in the results.

cat_activity.note: NLM tags CI/CD automation, team size and feature complexity as Activity, but none is a repository activity count.

cat_delivery.note: Release Cycle Duration (first commit to deployment) is the target variable.

cat_devex.note: Cognitive load (context switching) and feedback modelled as DX metrics, grounded in the DX framework of Greiler, Storey and Noda (2022: flow, cognitive load, feedback loops), not the 2023 Noda/Storey/Forsgren paper; variables are author-defined.

cat_agile.note: Feature scope in story points as scenario variable; 14-day threshold based on two-week sprints.

cat_survey.note: Subjective ordinal (1-5) ratings defined as survey-based (e.g., B obtained from a survey), but values are synthetic; no survey administered.

evidence.quote: A simulation model was developed for this analysis, embodying a prototypical CI/CD infrastructure characterized by either a microservices or serverless architecture within a cloud framework.
Synthetic data was generated to simulate a typical DevOps development cycle under controlled experimental conditions.
Two baseline models were implemented: linear regression and random forest regression.
RCD (Release Cycle Duration) - the duration of the release cycle, defined as the time interval between the first commit of a feature and its successful deployment.
B (Developer Tooling Satisfaction) - a subjective assessment of satisfaction with engineering tools (IDE, CI/CD services, build, etc.); obtained from a survey.
C (Communication Quality) - an assessment of the effectiveness of intra-team communication during the release.
F (Feedback from Code Review) - a feedback indicator: timeliness, quality, and usefulness of reviews from other developers.
The DX model proposed in [17] focuses on three key components: flow, cognitive load, and feedback loops.
H1. Increased cognitive load, poor quality engineering tools, and reduced feedback lead to a statistically significant increase in release cycle length.
Adapting Agile practices, in particular iterative development with a small volume of tasks in each sprint, allows to reduce the probability of delay by 42 percentage points
